newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on BSE rumors, export signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on BSE rumors, export signals.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed sharply lower on a wire service report an Indiana farmer may have died from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), a human version of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) or "mad cow" disease, traders said.
A scare about U.S. beef could cut into consumption of beef and in turn, livestock feed, especially corn, sources said.

However, the Indiana Health Department said it could not confirm press reports that the death of a 62-year-old Indiana man was from Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), but said the state has several cases of CJD annually.
Exports, weather and technicals also were cited.
There were concerns about a slowdown in exports of U.S. corn which this week were given credence by confirmation that Taiwan would cut back on its imports.

USDA this week said Taiwan would import the smallest amount of corn in three years at 5.83 million tonnes, below the previous estimate for 6.33 million. The cut was due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan.
Corn closed three to 6-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 5-1/2 at $2.97-1/4.
Traders also said corn was in a technical slide. Also, outlooks for better seeding weather in the Midwest were noted.

"You've got decent weather coming through the Midwest," said Brian Scott, head of floor operations for R.J. O'Brien. "There's rain forecast for the weekend. Guys may take the opportunity to get some (corn) in the ground."
Technicians pointed out that July fell below its 40-day moving average of roughly $3.00 per bushel which was viewed as a significant break.
"It closed below it (40-day MA) so I would expect to see more liquidation tomorrow, but exports will be the driving force," a trader said.
USDA at 0730 CDT Thursday will release its latest weekly export sales report.
There were expectations for the corn export tally to total between 500,000 to 700,000 tonnes.
Refco Inc was the key seller of at least 25 million bushels of corn, eight million in the July and 17.0 million in the December, traders said.
Cargill Inc bought ten million bushels of December and Farmers Commodities Corp sold 2.5 million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 70,000 contracts, above the 67,777 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, Lind Waldock bought 1,500 July $2.70 puts at three cents, bought 1,200 July $3.50 calls at 2-3/4, sold 1,200 July $3.20 calls at 6-1/2 cents and bought 1,200 July $2.70 puts at three cents, traders said.

In spread trading, Goldenberg Hehmeyer did five million bushels of July/May at 1-3/4 cents, premium July, LIT America spread two million July/May at 1-3/4 cents, premium July and E.D. and F. Man International spread three million May/July at 1-3/4 cents, premium July.
Corn options volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, above the 15,630 traded Tuesday.
